summary: @servicetitan/kendo-theme preinstall fetches Bun runtime and executes obfuscated bundled payload
details: Package presents itself as a Kendo UI CSS theme (main is dist/index.css and src contains only.scss sources), but package.json declares "preinstall": "node setup.mjs". setup.mjs is an obfuscator.io-style script (hex-named identifiers _0x488df8/_0x52943e, property-shuffled dispatch objects) that downloads the Bun runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/... and then invokes execFileSync on the downloaded Bun binary against a bundled 727KB file math_init.js. math_init.js is a Bun-compiled bundle (// @bun @bun-cjs header) with a rotated string/opcode table (n7gIxM numeric array, WV8StW rotator, hc1jfK9 decoder) and hex-scrambled identifiers, so all strings and any network destinations are reconstructed at runtime. A CSS theme has no need for a second language runtime or a compiled executable payload; the shape is an alternate-runtime dropper that executes attacker-controlled obfuscated code on the installer's machine at npm install time, evading Node-only static inspection. The @servicetitan scope also suggests brand impersonation.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
